description: California delta. Facts checked against the California Driver Handbook (dmv.ca.gov) alcohol, provisional-license, and negligent-operator sections.

questions.q: In California, a driver 21 or older is illegally impaired at a BAC of
questions.explanation: The handbook states it is illegal to drive at 0.08% or higher if you are over 21.
questions.why: Alcohol affects your ability to drive safely.

questions.q: In California, a driver under 21 may not drive at a BAC of
questions.explanation: The handbook lists 0.01% or higher as illegal if you are under 21.

questions.q: A driver on DUI probation in California is limited to a BAC of
questions.explanation: The handbook says 0.01% or higher is illegal at any age if you are on DUI probation.

questions.q: During the first 12 months, a provisional licensee may not carry passengers under 20 unless
questions.explanation: The passenger restriction bars passengers under 20 unless a parent, guardian, or licensed driver 25 or older is in the car, or another listed exception applies.
questions.remember: First year: no young riders without an adult.

questions.q: Three at-fault collisions or convictions (or a combination) for a minor lead to
questions.explanation: The handbook says the driving privilege is suspended for six months and the driver is on probation for one year. Turning 18 does not erase that action.
questions.remember: Three strikes: six months off the road.

provenance.section: Laws and Rules of the Road — minors

questions.q: California treats you as a negligent operator if you get
questions.explanation: The handbook: an adult's license may be suspended at 4 points in 12 months, 6 points in 24 months, or 8 points in 36 months.

questions.q: Unless a different limit is posted, the maximum speed on most California highways is
questions.explanation: The handbook states the maximum on most California highways is 65 mph.

questions.q: The prima facie speed in a California school zone when children are present is
questions.explanation: The handbook: the speed limit is 25 mph within 500 feet of a school while children are outside or crossing the street.

questions.q: The prima facie speed limit in a California alley is
questions.explanation: The handbook lists 15 mph as the speed limit in an alley.

questions.q: At a blind intersection in a residential district, the California prima facie limit is
questions.explanation: The handbook: the speed limit for a blind intersection is 15 mph. An intersection is blind if it has no stop signs at any corner.

questions.q: How old must you be to apply for an instruction permit if you are under 18?
questions.explanation: Applicants under 18 must be at least 15 1/2 years old to apply for a California instruction permit.

questions.q: Before scheduling the behind-the-wheel drive test, a minor must hold their instruction permit for a minimum of:
questions.explanation: A minor needs to have held a permit (from California or another state) for six months or more, or reach 18, before booking the drive test.

questions.q: Before getting a driver's license, a teen driver must complete at least 50 hours of practice driving. How many of those hours must take place at night?
questions.explanation: Of the 50 hours of required practice driving for minors, at least 10 hours must be completed at night.
questions.why: At night, motorcycles, pedestrians, and bicyclists are much harder to see.

questions.q: When completing the mandatory 50 hours of practice driving for a minor's license, the supervising California-licensed driver must be at least:
questions.explanation: A minor's 50 practice hours must be supervised by a California-licensed driver aged 25 or older.

questions.q: If a minor fails the driver's license knowledge exam, how long are they required to wait before attempting it again?
options: Three days, not counting the day they failed
Seven days, not counting the day they failed
Fourteen days, not counting the day they failed
Thirty days, not counting the day they failed
questions.explanation: Minors are required to wait seven days to retake a failed knowledge test, which does not include the day the failure occurred.

questions.q: If a minor does not pass the behind-the-wheel driving test, what is the mandatory waiting period before they can take it again?
questions.explanation: A minor who fails the drive test has to wait 14 days, not counting the day of the failed test, before trying again.

questions.q: During your behind-the-wheel driving test, what is the rule regarding backup cameras and blind spot monitors?
options: They must be completely covered or turned off.
You can rely on them entirely for backing up and changing lanes.
They are strictly forbidden and will cause an automatic failure.
You may use them, but must still check mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Backup cameras and blind spot monitors are allowed on the drive test, but you still have to look at your mirrors and blind spots yourself.
questions.why: Cameras and monitors do not replace a visual check of your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.q: If you move to a new home, within how many days must you report your updated address to the DMV?
questions.explanation: If you change your address, California law requires you to notify the DMV within ten days.

questions.q: What happens if you wear glasses or contact lenses while passing your DMV vision exam?
options: You will need to take a secondary vision test without them.
A corrective lenses restriction will be placed on your driver's license.
You must provide a note from an eye doctor before driving.
Your license will only be valid for daytime driving.
questions.explanation: Taking the vision test with corrective or contact lenses results in a corrective lenses restriction on your final driver's license.
questions.remember: Test with glasses, drive with glasses.

questions.q: Can you use a vehicle's automated parallel parking or adaptive cruise control features during the behind-the-wheel test?
options: Yes, as long as you inform the examiner before the test begins.
Yes, because evaluating the vehicle's technology is part of the test.
No, these advanced assistance systems are not permitted during the test.
Only if the examiner explicitly asks you to demonstrate them.
questions.explanation: The drive test evaluates your driving abilities, not the vehicle's technology. Advanced systems like automated parallel parking or adaptive cruise control are not allowed.
questions.why: The test checks your skill at driving, not the vehicle's technology.
questions.remember: Drive test: you drive, not the car.

questions.q: To take the behind-the-wheel test, your vehicle's tires must have a minimum uniform tread depth of:
questions.explanation: During the pre-drive vehicle inspection, the examiner will verify that your tires have at least 1/32-inch of uniformed tread depth.

questions.q: If you are an adult applying for a driver's license, the California-licensed driver who rides with you while you practice must be at least how old?
questions.explanation: An adult permit holder may practice with a California-licensed driver 18 or older; minors need a supervisor 25 or older.

questions.q: Is it legal to store an opened container of alcohol in the glove box of your vehicle?
options: Yes, as long as the glove box is locked with a key.
Yes, provided the container is securely capped.
No, an open container cannot be kept there.
Only if the driver is over 21 years of age.
questions.explanation: If an alcohol container has been opened, you must keep it in the trunk or a place where passengers do not sit. It is illegal to keep an open container in your glove box.

questions.q: The law prohibiting open alcohol containers in a vehicle does not apply to passengers riding in which of the following?
options: A friend's personal car or truck
A rental car on a road trip
A taxi, bus, camper, or motorhome
questions.explanation: The strict laws regarding carrying open alcohol containers do not apply to passengers in a bus, taxi, camper, or motorhome.

questions.q: By driving in California, you automatically consent to which type of test if suspected of driving under the influence?
options: A breath, blood, or urine test
A vehicle search for illegal substances
A roadside vision and cognitive exam
questions.explanation: California's implied consent rule means driving in the state counts as agreeing to a breath, blood, or urine test when an officer suspects DUI.
questions.remember: Drive here, agree to the test.

questions.q: What will happen to your driving privilege if a law enforcement officer asks you to take a blood or urine test for drugs and you refuse?
options: You will be issued a warning and a fine.
Your driving privilege will be suspended or revoked for one year.
Your vehicle will be immediately impounded for 30 days.
You will be required to retake the written and driving exams.
questions.explanation: If an officer believes you are driving under the influence and asks for a blood or urine test, refusing leads DMV to suspend or revoke your driving privilege for one year.
questions.remember: Say no to the test, lose the license.

questions.q: If you are under 21 and caught driving with an alcoholic beverage in your vehicle without an adult age 21 or older present, how long can law enforcement impound your car?
questions.explanation: If a minor is caught with alcohol in their vehicle while driving unaccompanied by an adult 21 or older, law enforcement can impound the vehicle for up to 30 days.

questions.q: If an unlicensed driver under the age of 21 is caught with alcohol in their vehicle, how might this affect their ability to get a license?
options: They will be permanently barred from getting a license.
They must wait until they turn 21 to apply.
They will have to pass the drive test twice.
Their first license may be delayed up to one year.
questions.explanation: If a minor does not yet have a driver's license and is caught with alcohol in their vehicle, the court can ask the DMV to delay giving them their first license for up to one year.

questions.q: If a driver under 21 years old is convicted of a DUI with a Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.01% or higher, they will be required to:
options: Surrender their vehicle to the state.
questions.explanation: A driver under 21 convicted of DUI at 0.01% BAC or more can lose the license for a year and must finish a licensed DUI program.

questions.q: In California, what is the minimum required insurance coverage amount for a single death or injury?
questions.explanation: California's minimum liability coverage is $30,000 for the death or injury of one person.

questions.q: California law requires your auto insurance to cover at least what amount for property damage?
questions.explanation: Insurance in California must cover at least $15,000 for property damage.

questions.q: If you are involved in a collision and do not have the proper insurance coverage, your driving privilege can be suspended for up to:
questions.explanation: Being in a collision without proper insurance can cost you your driving privilege for up to four years, no matter who caused the crash.

questions.q: If you are involved in a collision where someone is injured or killed, within what timeframe must you make a report to law enforcement?
questions.explanation: When a collision injures or kills anyone, it must be reported to police within 24 hours.

questions.q: What should you do if your vehicle rolls into a parked car and you cannot locate the owner?
options: Leave and let the owner contact your insurer later.
Leave a secure note with your contact info and notify police.
Wait beside the car for as long as it takes the owner to return.
Photograph the damage and drive away without leaving a note.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, securely attach a note with your name, phone number, and address, and report the collision to law enforcement.
questions.remember: Hit a parked car: note and report.

questions.q: You must report a collision to the DMV within 10 days if anyone was injured or killed, or if the property damage exceeds:
questions.explanation: A DMV report is due within 10 days when property damage tops $1,000 or anyone is hurt or killed.

questions.q: After a collision that must be reported, who has to file the SR 1 accident report with DMV?
options: Only the driver who caused the collision.
The law enforcement officer who arrives at the scene.
You or your representative, regardless of who was at fault.
questions.explanation: You or your representative must file the SR 1 report with the DMV regardless of whether or not you caused the collision. Law enforcement will not make this specific report for you.

questions.q: If you are under 21 and a preliminary alcohol screening (PAS) shows a BAC of 0.05% or higher, what can the officer require you to do next?
options: Take a formal breath or blood test.
Surrender your vehicle immediately on the spot.
Pay a traffic citation and drive home.
questions.explanation: If a PAS test shows a BAC of 0.05% or higher for an underage driver, the officer may then require a full breath or blood test.

questions.q: How long does a DUI conviction remain on your California driver's record?
questions.explanation: A DUI conviction stays on a California driving record for 10 years, and another DUI in that period can bring extra penalties.

questions.q: If you are arrested for a DUI, the officer may confiscate your driver's license and issue you a temporary one that is valid for how many days?
questions.explanation: After a DUI arrest the officer may take your license and issue a temporary one good for 30 days.

questions.q: Following a DUI arrest, you have a limited window to request a DMV administrative hearing to challenge your license suspension. How long is this window?
options: 5 days from the date of your arrest.
14 days from the date of your arrest.
30 days from the date of your arrest.
10 days from the date of your arrest.
questions.explanation: You have 10 days from the arrest date to ask DMV for an administrative hearing.
questions.remember: Arrested? 10 days to ask for a hearing.

questions.q: After selling your vehicle, how soon must you notify DMV with a Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability?
questions.explanation: California requires you to notify the DMV within five days when you sell a vehicle.

questions.q: If you purchase a vehicle, how many days do you have to transfer the ownership into your name?
questions.explanation: A buyer has 10 days to put the vehicle's ownership in their own name.

questions.q: After moving to California or getting a job in the state, how many days do you have to register your out-of-state vehicle?
questions.explanation: You are given 20 days to register your vehicle after becoming a California resident or obtaining employment in the state.

questions.q: If a law enforcement officer issues you a Notice of Priority Reexamination, how many days do you have to contact the DMV before your license is automatically suspended?
questions.explanation: When issued a Notice of Priority Reexamination, you must contact the DMV to initiate the process within five working days, or your driving privilege will be automatically suspended.
questions.remember: Priority reexam: call in 5 working days.

questions.q: If you accidentally hit and injure an animal on the road, what is the proper course of action?
options: Call the nearest humane society or law enforcement, and do not try to move it.
Carefully load the animal into your car and drive it to a vet.
Move the animal to the side of the road and continue driving.
Honk your horn to scare the animal out of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If you kill or injure an animal, you should call the nearest humane society or law enforcement and avoid trying to move the injured animal yourself.

questions.q: A provisional driver may drive during restricted hours for a medical need if they carry a physician's note. What specific information must this note contain?
options: A full list of prescribed medications
The condition and expected recovery date
The doctor's home phone number and address
Proof of current health insurance coverage
questions.explanation: For a medical need exception to provisional restrictions, the physician's note must include your medical condition and the date you are expected to recover.
questions.remember: Doctor's note: condition and recovery date.

questions.q: In California, what is the BAC limit for a driver who is carrying a passenger for hire?
questions.explanation: California sets a 0.04% BAC limit for anyone driving a passenger for hire, lower than the 0.08% limit for ordinary drivers over 21.

questions.q: Which of the following can legally prompt the DMV to reexamine your ability to drive safely?
options: Reaching the age of 75, regardless of your driving record.
Upgrading your vehicle to a newer model with advanced technology.
Simply your age, starting at 70 years old.
A physical or mental condition or a poor driving record, not age.
questions.explanation: The DMV can investigate your driving ability based on a physical or mental condition or a poor driver's record, but age alone is not a valid basis for a reexamination.

questions.q: You are driving on a road and see two sets of solid double yellow lines that are spaced two or more feet apart. Are you allowed to cross them?
options: Yes, but only if you are passing a slow-moving vehicle.
Yes, if you are entering a private driveway.
No, unless you are making a U-turn.
No, except at a designated opening.
questions.explanation: Two sets of double yellow lines at least two feet apart form a barrier. You may cross it, even for a left turn or U-turn, only at a designated opening.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true regarding a center left-turn lane?
options: You can use it as a regular driving lane during heavy traffic.
You may drive in it for no more than 200 feet before making a turn.
It is used exclusively to pass slow-moving vehicles.
You can drive in this lane for up to 500 feet before turning.
questions.explanation: A center left-turn lane is designated for preparing to make a left turn or a U-turn. California law prohibits driving in this lane for more than 200 feet.

questions.q: Under California law, you must pull into a turnout area or lane to let others pass if you are driving slowly on a two-lane road and are being followed by:
questions.explanation: If passing is unsafe on a two-lane road and you are driving slowly with five or more vehicles stuck behind you, you are legally required to use a turnout area to let them pass.

questions.q: When making a right turn, you are allowed to enter and drive in a designated bicycle lane for up to how many feet before the intersection?
questions.explanation: You may not drive in a bicycle lane unless you are preparing for a turn, or entering/leaving the road. When turning, you can enter the bike lane up to 200 feet before the intersection.
questions.remember: Bike lane: enter only to turn.

questions.q: When waiting to make a left turn, why should you keep your steering wheel pointed straight ahead?
options: It decreases the time it takes to complete the turn.
It prevents unnecessary wear on your power steering.
It is legally required to avoid blocking the intersection.
It prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.
questions.explanation: If your wheels are turned to the left while you wait to turn and another vehicle rear-ends you, the impact could push your vehicle directly into oncoming traffic.
questions.why: If your wheels point left and you are hit from behind, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.q: In California, it is legal to make a left turn at a solid red traffic light only if you are turning:
options: One-way street onto another one-way street.
Two-way street onto a one-way street.
One-way street onto a two-way street.
Under no circumstances; it is always illegal.
questions.explanation: California allows a left turn on a red light only when going from one one-way street onto another, if no sign forbids it and you yield to traffic and pedestrians.
questions.remember: Left on red: one-way to one-way.

questions.q: When is it legal to make a U-turn in a business district?
options: Anytime there is no oncoming traffic within 200 feet.
Mid-block, after signaling for at least 100 feet.
Only at an intersection or a designated opening on a divided highway.
It is never legal to make a U-turn in a business district.
questions.explanation: U-turns are generally prohibited in business districts. You may only make one at an intersection or where an opening is specifically provided on a divided highway.
questions.remember: Business district: U-turn at intersections only.

questions.q: When making a U-turn in a residential district, you must ensure there are no approaching vehicles within:
questions.explanation: In a residential district, U-turns are legal as long as no other vehicles are approaching you within 200 feet, or if you are at an intersection controlled by a traffic sign or light.

questions.q: It is illegal to pass another vehicle within how many feet of an intersection, bridge, or railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of hazardous areas such as intersections, bridges, tunnels, and railroad crossings where your visibility or maneuvering space is limited.
questions.remember: Near crossings and bridges: don't pass.

questions.q: When you have properly parallel parked your vehicle, your wheels must be within how many inches of the curb?
questions.explanation: After parallel parking, your vehicle should be parallel to the roadway and its wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb.

questions.q: A yellow painted curb indicates that parking is:
options: Allowed only to load or unload people or freight.
Reserved for public transit buses only.
questions.explanation: A yellow curb means you may stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight. You generally must stay with your vehicle unless it is a commercial vehicle.

questions.q: A painted green curb means you may:
options: Park if you have a zero-emission vehicle.
questions.explanation: Green curbs indicate that you can park there for a limited time. The specific time limit is usually posted on nearby signs or painted on the curb itself.

questions.q: A red painted curb means:
options: You may stop to load or unload freight only.
You may stop to pick up passengers.
You may park for up to 15 minutes.
questions.explanation: Red curbs mean no stopping, standing, or parking is allowed under any circumstances, though buses may sometimes stop at red zones marked for them.

questions.q: You may never park your vehicle within how many feet of a fire hydrant or fire station driveway?
questions.explanation: California law strictly prohibits parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or the driveway of a fire station to ensure emergency vehicles have immediate access.

questions.q: If you are forced to stop your vehicle on a freeway shoulder due to an emergency, it may be towed or removed if left standing for more than:
questions.explanation: A vehicle left on a California freeway for longer than four hours may be removed, so park fully off the pavement and get help.

questions.q: When a law enforcement officer turns on their emergency lights to pull you over, what is the first thing you should do?
options: Turn on your right turn signal.
Get out and walk back to the officer.
questions.explanation: The first action to take during a law enforcement stop is to turn on your right turn signal to acknowledge the officer, then safely move to the right shoulder.
questions.why: Signaling right shows the officer you have seen them.

questions.q: At a crosswalk, a blind pedestrian draws the cane back and moves away from the corner. What does this usually mean?
options: They are signaling that you may go.
They are waiting for you to honk before they cross.
They need you to exit your vehicle and assist them.
They dropped something and will cross shortly.
questions.explanation: When a blind person pulls their cane inward and steps back from the crosswalk, this gesture usually means they are yielding the right-of-way and you may proceed.
questions.remember: Cane pulled back: you may go.

questions.q: When two vehicles meet on a steep, narrow mountain road where neither can pass, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: The uphill vehicle has the right-of-way. The downhill driver can control the car better while reversing uphill, so that driver backs up until the other can pass.
questions.why: The vehicle facing downhill has more control when backing up the hill.

questions.q: At 55 mph, a large commercial truck can take up to how many feet to come to a complete stop?
questions.explanation: Large trucks and commercial vehicles take much longer to stop than passenger cars. At 55 mph, while a car needs about 300 feet, a large vehicle may need up to 400 feet.
questions.why: Large vehicles take longer to stop than cars at the same speed.

questions.q: When passing a bus or streetcar that is stopped at a safety zone, you must do so at a speed no greater than:
questions.explanation: If a bus, streetcar, or trolley is stopped at a safety zone or traffic light, you are required to slow down and pass at no more than 10 mph.
questions.why: Safety zones are for people waiting for buses, streetcars, and trolleys.

questions.q: When a fire engine, ambulance, or police car has its siren or flashing lights on, how far behind it must you stay?
questions.explanation: California law prohibits driving within 300 feet behind any emergency vehicle that is responding to an emergency with its sirens or flashing lights active.

questions.q: Neighborhood Electric Vehicles (NEVs) are restricted from being driven on roads where the speed limit exceeds:
questions.explanation: NEVs and Low-Speed Vehicles (LSVs) can only reach a maximum speed of 25 mph and are prohibited from operating on roadways with a speed limit greater than 35 mph.

questions.q: When riding a bicycle at night, your bicycle must be equipped with a front lamp emitting a white light visible from a distance of at least:
questions.explanation: Nighttime bicyclists are required to have a front lamp with a white light that is visible from at least 300 feet away.
questions.remember: Bike at night: white light ahead.

questions.q: When passing a bicyclist traveling in your lane, you must allow at least how much space between your vehicle and the bicyclist?
questions.explanation: California law mandates that you give bicyclists at least three feet of clearance when passing. If you cannot provide three feet, you must wait until it is safe to do so.
questions.why: Bicyclists need room so they are not forced into parked cars or open doors.

questions.q: What is the penalty for committing a traffic violation in a highway construction zone when workers are present?
options: Your license is suspended for 30 days.
You receive a warning for the first offense.
questions.explanation: Fines for traffic violations are doubled in highway construction or maintenance zones whenever workers are present.
questions.why: Workers and slow-moving equipment may be close to traffic.

questions.q: If you are towing a trailer on a freeway with four lanes in your direction, which lanes are you allowed to use?
options: The two lanes closest to the right edge.
Any lane as long as you drive the speed limit.
The two lanes closest to the center divider.
questions.explanation: Vehicles towing trailers or trucks with three or more axles must drive in the far-right lane. If there are four or more lanes, they may use the two lanes closest to the right edge.

questions.q: You are driving on a divided highway and see a school bus stopped on the opposite side with its red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
Slow to 15 mph and proceed with caution.
Stop and wait for the bus driver to wave you through.
You do not need to stop because you are on a divided highway.
questions.explanation: California does not require you to stop when the bus is across a divided highway, or a highway with two or more lanes in each direction.
questions.remember: Divided road: other side can keep going.

questions.q: Failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights can result in:
questions.explanation: Not stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights can bring a fine of up to $1,000 and a one-year suspension of your driving privilege.
questions.why: Children may be crossing the street around a stopped school bus.
questions.remember: Red lights on the bus: stop.

questions.q: When a crossing device or a person warns you that a train is approaching a railroad crossing, you must stop at least how far from the nearest track?
questions.explanation: If warned of an approaching train, you are legally required to stop at least 15 feet from the nearest track to maintain a safe distance.

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a business or residential district?
questions.explanation: In California, the default speed limit in business or residential districts is 25 mph unless a different speed limit is explicitly posted.

questions.q: If you carry cargo that extends more than 4 feet beyond your rear bumper, what must you do?
options: Paint the end of the cargo bright yellow.
Turn on your emergency flashers at all times.
Attach a red or fluorescent orange flag, 12 inches square.
You may not carry cargo that extends beyond 3 feet.
questions.explanation: Cargo sticking out more than 4 feet past the rear bumper needs a 12-inch square red or fluorescent orange flag, and two red lights at night.

questions.q: Is it legal to transport an animal in the back of a pickup truck?
options: Yes, but only if you drive below 25 mph.
No, animals must always ride in the passenger cab.
Yes, but only on residential streets.
Yes, if the animal is properly secured.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to transport animals in the back of a pickup truck unless they are properly secured in a manner that prevents them from falling, jumping, or being thrown from the vehicle.
questions.why: This keeps the animal from falling, jumping, or being thrown out.
questions.remember: Pets in the pickup: tie them in.

questions.q: Where is the only legal place you can affix an electronic toll payment device on your windshield?
options: A 5-inch square in the center uppermost portion.
A 7-inch square on the upper passenger's side.
Directly in the center of the windshield.
A 5-inch square on the lower center portion.
questions.explanation: An electronic toll device may only go in a 5-inch square at the top center of the windshield, where it does not block your view.
questions.why: The windshield must give you a full, clear view of the road.

questions.q: In California, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: California issues a learner's permit for a car at 15½ years at the earliest.
questions.remember: California car permit: 15½ years at the earliest.

questions.q: In California, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: California requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in California complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: California requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: In California, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In California, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in California not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: California restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: California new drivers: off the road 11 p.m. to 5 a.m..

questions.q: How many questions are on the California car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The California car knowledge test has 46 questions.

provenance.manual: Evaluation of the Class C Driver License Written Knowledge Tests - California DMV

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the California car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 83% to pass the California car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Evaluation of the Class C Driver License Written Knowledge Tests - California DMV

questions.q: In California, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in California brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: California, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

provenance.manual: Section 9: Alcohol and Drugs - California DMV

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in California?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in California can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: California rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes California's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: California: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in California?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In California, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: California left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is California's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: California seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in California?
questions.explanation: California requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: California: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: Under California's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: California can suspend an adult's license at 4 points in 12 months.
